prds.title: Product & workspace
prds.problem: A plugin idea, its requirements and its implementation context are otherwise scattered across tools.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin developers, product owners and designers.
prds.goals:
One vault owns one project
Capture requirements and acceptance
Author screens and transitions
Declare domain relationships
Use reusable components
Select blueprints and patterns
prds.nonGoals: No native conversion, live service access or release authorization from the browser concept.

requirements.title: One vault owns one project
requirements.acceptance: Opening this workspace exposes one project; loading another definition requires review and never adds a second active project.

requirements.title: Capture requirements and acceptance
requirements.acceptance: Create, revise, map and export PRDs with testable requirements, priorities and retained review baselines.

requirements.title: Author screens and transitions
requirements.acceptance: Edit screens, containers, content sections and transitions with keyboard and pointer controls, Undo and Redo.

requirements.title: Declare domain relationships
requirements.acceptance: Define properties and explicit cardinalities while keeping diagram arrangement separate from persistence semantics.

requirements.title: Use reusable components
requirements.acceptance: Place pinned component versions and variants with local content; preview and deliberately apply upgrades.

requirements.title: Select blueprints and patterns
requirements.acceptance: Use a reviewed starter and shared action patterns without overwriting an existing design silently.

prds.title: Data & visual contracts
prds.problem: Developers need explicit data and visual contracts before implementation can be safely generated.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin developers, product owners and designers.
prds.goals:
Describe every source port
Reuse source operations
Generate deterministic test data
Exercise isolated operations
Export isolated test tooling
Author the design system
Export a readable design guide
prds.nonGoals: No native conversion, live service access or release authorization from the browser concept.

requirements.title: Describe every source port
requirements.acceptance: Vault, API and database declarations include operations and explicit input/output shapes; credentials remain symbolic.

requirements.title: Reuse source operations
requirements.acceptance: A screen references a declared source operation through a named directional data flow, not a duplicate source definition.

requirements.title: Generate deterministic test data
requirements.acceptance: Equal seed, schema and fixed reference date yield equal fixtures. No operation contacts a live source as fallback.

requirements.title: Exercise isolated operations
requirements.acceptance: Run and cancel a simulation, retain focus and distinguish status announcements from result payloads.

requirements.title: Export isolated test tooling
requirements.acceptance: Export fixtures and adapters with a read-only plan and explicit ownership checks before applying or cleaning files.

requirements.title: Author the design system
requirements.acceptance: Persist font declarations, typography, sizes, spacing, radii, paired colors, usage guidance and explicit Nuxt UI token bindings.

requirements.title: Export a readable design guide
requirements.acceptance: Markdown and offline HTML contain all saved declarations and disclose unevaluated contrast pairs. A scoped stylesheet export and the JSON-driven shell generator compile the same saved Nuxt UI token bindings.

prds.title: Project JSON & shell handoff
prds.problem: A developer needs one complete portable definition that both the design tool and shell can read.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin developers, product owners and designers.
prds.goals:
Describe the companion itself
Export the complete saved project
Import a full project safely
Configure project folders
Accept JSON at the shell boundary
Keep generation a separate stage
prds.nonGoals: No native conversion, live service access or release authorization from the browser concept.

requirements.title: Describe the companion itself
requirements.acceptance: The bundled companion project uses the same editable model, screens, requirements, entities, sources and design system as user projects.

requirements.title: Export the complete saved project
requirements.acceptance: The versioned JSON preserves identity, folder settings, PRDs, screen content, variants, arrangements, entities, source operations, test recipes, tokens and notes.

requirements.title: Import a full project safely
requirements.acceptance: File and pasted JSON are bounded and validated before review; invalid input, cancelled review or stale state leaves the project unchanged.

requirements.title: Configure project folders
requirements.acceptance: Codebase defaults to src and tests to tests. Valid custom folders persist and survive a JSON round trip; invalid or overlapping paths are rejected.

requirements.title: Accept JSON at the shell boundary
requirements.acceptance: The v1 script accepts the export and a target inside an explicitly selected vault, prints original JSON bytes, and performs zero filesystem writes.

requirements.title: Keep generation a separate stage
requirements.acceptance: The independent companion:scaffold / shell generate compiler reviews an ownership-safe apply plan, including compiled design-system styles. The read-only version-one handoff remains write-free.

prds.title: Storymaps & scope planning
prds.problem: A flat set of requirements loses the user experience and the intended scope of a useful release.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin developers, product owners and designers.
prds.goals:
Create and open storymaps from either entry point
Plan structured user experiences
Connect without copying artifacts
Plan outcome-oriented release slices
Transfer storymaps without data loss
prds.nonGoals: No native conversion, live service access or release authorization from the browser concept.

requirements.title: Create and open storymaps from either entry point
requirements.acceptance: Navigation and linked PRD details open the same map; returning retains the originating context.

requirements.title: Plan structured user experiences
requirements.acceptance: Activities, steps and stories keep semantic order across drag, form moves and shared Undo/Redo. Repeated story entry retains the destination; search preserves the complete map.

requirements.title: Connect without copying artifacts
requirements.acceptance: Items link existing sitemap identities and requirements. Searchable pickers retain selected references; direct links and Back preserve context. Missing targets remain explicit; linked artifacts are never deleted.

requirements.title: Plan outcome-oriented release slices
requirements.acceptance: Move stories between releases or Unplanned. Removing a release preserves its stories. Review surfaces missing outcomes, acceptance notes and targets without claiming implementation; archived maps require restore before editing.

requirements.title: Transfer storymaps without data loss
requirements.acceptance: Versioned project JSON preserves IDs, order, content, releases and references. Legacy projects are accepted without inventing stories.

prds.title: Safety & qualification
prds.problem: A convincing prototype must not imply that simulated execution or stored data is native evidence.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin developers, product owners and designers.
prds.goals:
Preserve drafts and keyboard context
Protect recovery copies
Keep test-vault boundaries
Keep verification scopes separate
Teach the complete workflow
Publish only after native acceptance
prds.nonGoals: No native conversion, live service access or release authorization from the browser concept.

requirements.title: Preserve drafts and keyboard context
requirements.acceptance: Closing dirty forms asks for confirmation; modal feedback is visible and focus returns to a meaningful control.

requirements.title: Protect recovery copies
requirements.acceptance: A stale window cannot reset newer retained state; current and retained data can be exported separately before reload.

requirements.title: Keep test-vault boundaries
requirements.acceptance: Authoring files, host configuration and test-target data are preserved; no silent path migration or plugin activation.

requirements.title: Keep verification scopes separate
requirements.acceptance: Build, browser, native and security evidence have explicit scope and revision. Import never grants trust or carries simulated passes forward.

requirements.title: Teach the complete workflow
requirements.acceptance: A dismissible and resumable guided tour covers all main design, test and preparation stages.

requirements.title: Publish only after native acceptance
requirements.acceptance: Shell qualification comes first, then native companion conversion and acceptance, then publication. No design action publishes.

# Companion implementation boundary

Shell qualification precedes native companion conversion. Publication is last. The first project-handoff script validates and returns JSON only; no boilerplate is generated by that script yet.
